author: Bigsmerf
subject: Tauren Rogues...?
content_md:
Just for clarification, this post is almost entirely for the sake of memeing. I'm not here to recommend, ask for, or demand any significant changes or changes at all, just some neat theorycrafting that may or may not be either underpowered or broken.

Starting off, why the heck would tauren become rogues? Well, anyone can wear leather armor and (attempt) to be sneaky or agile. 'nuff said.

Now, I think that obviously, given their stature, and build, tauren are not the best race for sneaking. With this in mind, I've decided to completely remove the ability to do so altogether! Now, you're probably asking "Wait, what? How do they use stealth abilities then?" Well, the answer is simply to give them a 'stealth', but allow them to be seen in this state. They will retain the slow move speed, and have a longer cooldown than regular stealth, but there could be some sort of compensation. Buffing the effects/damage in comparison to other rogues, or something similar comes to mind. I'm thinking of calling this "stealth" something like 'poise', wherein they prepare themselves to strike, like a bull kicking his hooves back.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: What increases your attack and casting speed by X% mean?
content_md:
How much worth attackspeed is varies from class to class and on how good the rest of your gear is.

Factors like your weaponspeed vs your spells cooldown als factor in. Paladins & hunters with raptor- / holy strike in particular can mess up their rotation with too much/ too little attackspeed.

For each 100% attackspeed the swingtime/casttime gets halfed.

So lets say you have might of menethil with a 3.8 swingspeed. If you have +10% attackspeed your new swingspeed would be

 3.8 / 1.1 = 3.45seconds/swing

The general consensus for most melees seems to be that an equal amount of crit outperforms an equal amount of haste, as haste only affects autohits & hits impacted by swingtimers.

For casters its a slightly different matter, as the spells base castspeed is used to calculate the new castspeed. With any cast speed reduction being applyed afterwards. Particularly druids & elemental shamans can therefore make great use out of haste

author: Poxfox
subject: Re: What increases your attack and casting speed by X% mean?
content_md:
> **Likaleo wrote: Fri Apr 26, 2024 11:48 am**
> > He does not want it to compare to attack power. He wants to translate every stats to attackpower and compare two items based on that.
>
>   Ok but why?
>
>  Excel gives dps on each item why not compare that?

This is much later and I apologize but going off the raw dps of an item is a bad idea generally speaking in terms of optimizing. It's good for a lot, don't get me wrong but when you start playing with things like crit cap it gets a lot more convoluted. For example if you're above hitcap, but not pushing crit cap, then hit is effectively a near nil increase because it's only reducing auto miss chance which is always astronomically high, yet it gets the most benefit up to hit cap so you can never miss special attacks on bosses. Inversely if you're at the crit cap, Crit is now useless and Agility loses a huge chunk of its value, but Hit is now a premium. However, breaking an item into just attack power/AEP (Agility Equivalence Points) says "Okay, 1% of hit is worth having this much Agility, therefore this much DPS", that value wildly fluctuates based on where you are at so an item might read as giving more DPS than it actually gives to you.

There's a lot of hard to quantify silliness too, in Classic (Not Turtle) for example, rogues were swearing by our old spreadsheets on launch because "This gives you the most net attack power" despite the Classic hit crap being significantly lower (rogues needed 1% hit on gear with 305 skill) which drastically affected the values on things with hit because on private servers we were used to needing 8% on gear. Mask of the Unforgiven now is a novelty item instead of ridiculously strong. Then it becomes discovered Shadowcraft 6 set is actually REALLY good compared to what we thought. Stat-wise it was a complete joke, but the proc and proc rate were good enough that 6 set Shadowcraft was very much better than your pre-raid gear and it took being able to replace all 6 of those pieces at once to justify breaking it. To be fair, private servers have always hated Shadowcraft and given it a lower proc rate, Classic it felt a hell of a lot higher.

It's not as bad as it was in TBC though. TBC felt like changing one piece of gear after raid night meant you were needing to change everything else.

You also have fight to fight optimizations where for like Firemaw, you'd ideally try to run a fair bit of Fire Resistance as a melee just to reduce the amount of downtime you have resetting stacks, sometimes you never have to run out. That makes a lot of gear mathematically a pain in the ass to quantify but it all is technically "better" in that instance even without raw dps increases.

author: Gantulga
subject: Little suggestion regarding normalizing certain bonuses
content_md:
So right now we have multiple sources that boost certain attack skills but not others. It is very inconsistent and doesn't make much sense.

Lethality: boosts everything except Riposte.
Remorseless Attacks: doesn't work with Hemorrhage or Riposte.
Cold Blood: doesn't work with Ghostly Strike, Hemorrhage or Riposte.
Revealed Flaw (T3 bonus): doesn't work with Ghostly Strike, Ambush or Riposte.

Riposte is the main outlier which is sad since it's a very conditional skill, but it's inconsistent all around.

Wouldn't it be nice if all those bonuses were normalized to simply affect all instant physical damage abilities?

author: Gottabe
subject: Pros and cons being aliance/horde rogue
content_md:
Would be interesting to hear other people opinions about this, just my personal thoughts, but overall i think you shouldn't choose race or faction based on some superior perks, just enjoy esthetical aspect of game. Generally speaking about PVP:

As Horde rogue. most people choose undead or orc.

People choose orc for stun resist and bloodrage, which are amazing skills for pvp, especially stun resist... would help against other rogues or paladins, which you gonna face a lot, but it's kinda lottery thing :) but could save your life. If you got stunned by pally or other rogue, high chance that you're dead :) Only thing could help - consumables, but many players not willing spent money on them, especially during gearing process.
The other thing is facing human ability - perception, have to keep some distance or use vanish. Human rogues will have advantage finding you first.

Undead rogue, of course  WOTF, and generally esthetical aspect. Cannibalize also very underestimated skill :) WOTF amazing ability to counter fear. But you'll face all factors i mentioned above, forgot to mention dwarf racial ability, you always have to keep it in mind when use blind :)

As Aliance rogue most people choose human, dwarf or gnome.

Being human  is easier to detect stealth, but not always help with orc rogues, when your stun got resisted, could be total game changer, of course not in your favor :) Other good thing you don't need worry about paladins ) Most thing you have to deal is orc stun resistance racial.
Dwarf - good racial ability to remove bleeds, poisons and diseases, including blind from other rogues.
Gnome - good ability to escape slows and movement impairing effects.
Overall most annoying thing for alliance rogues is orc racial :)

I just mentioned some common situations you gonna face in bg's and world PVP, of course some things like engineering, consumables etc gives you huge advantage, but it's other story ;)

author: Akos1896
subject: Re: Stealing a Peek
content_md:
My answer will be very limited because I only did PVE with my rogue. No raiding either. Troll boy is currently around level 26 because I found the PVE gameplay boring and I haven't touched him for months. It means that I had less tools than a raiding rogue, what I saw was limited.
But telling what I heard and experienced.

PVP might be fun, I heard. Farming is okay, specially if you have some bandages. Dungeons were boring. Before making the rogue, I was imagining moving in the shadows, sapping mobs before pulls, being a utility and kick powerhouse, kinda a ninja. In theory, you can try sapping mobs before pull but unless you go to the PVP build, you'll probably lose stealth, everything attacks you and you are forced to use a reagent+CD ability to get back to the shadows. Tanks won't wait for your little show anyway, they'll just pull.
Once pull happens, you run to the mob, seek his backside and you start a mini game of energy, combo points and finishers. Sounds fun but was boring. You make sure you maintain the haste buff on yourself, maybe do some eviscerates, everything else is only there if you're fancy. Can expose armor but if there's a warrior in the party, they'll just automatically overwrite it with sunder all the time.
So you're hitting the backside of the foe and make a rotation 90% focused on keeping up a haste buff. Sometimes you can kick which is cool. But as I experienced, most of the rogue's fun is suppoed to be stealthing around and doing huge damage from a well-planned opening. Try this in a dungeon where the tank feels like being on cocaine and the hunter somehow pulls half of the region. At the end of the day dungeoning felt really boring. Looking for mobs' backside, auto-attacking. Sinister strike, auto-attack, keeping up haste, LF other enemy backside.
And your own professions... On paper sounds cool. In practice you need a reagent or material for everything. A rogue wants to shít, he needs a reagent to do it I swear. For example poisons are cool. But you make your doses in advance using materials and they expire super fast. On my enh shaman I just selected the weapon enhancement I liked and pressed it every 5 minute. You want to use half of your abilities? Reagent. You want to look like an orc peon? Materials. Every time you make the costume. Only lockpicking is different which just requires some tools to be in your bag. And also spending one of your Friday nights in a ship in the Barrens, interacting with a set of chests.

People also kinda boo internally every time you show up at the dungeon. Good damage, sure. But palas/shamans bring super buffs, a mage gives int, water, sheep etc, even a hunter can use traps. As a rogue you go to a dung 'bufflesly' and also rival most tanks at items. (I mean palas and warriors at weapons, drus at some leather items).

From raiding, I only heard about it. In theory it's chill with an easy rotation. But also, rogue is the only class which has no real upside at raids after BWL. From AQ40 a fury warrior is almost always better.

Again, for PVP I have no idea.

But telling what I heard and experienced.

PVP might be fun, I heard. Farming is okay, specially if you have some bandages. Dungeons were boring. Before making the rogue, I was imagining moving in the shadows, sapping mobs before pulls, being a utility and kick powerhouse, kinda a ninja. In theory, you can try sapping mobs before pull but unless you go to the PVP build, you'll probably lose stealth, everything attacks you and you are forced to use a reagent+CD ability to get back to the shadows. Tanks won't wait for your little show anyway, they'll just pull.
Once pull happens, you run to the mob, seek his backside and you start a mini game of energy, combo points and finishers. Sounds fun but was boring. You make sure you maintain the haste buff on yourself, maybe do some eviscerates, everything else is only there if you're fancy. Can expose armor but if there's a warrior in the party, they'll just automatically overwrite it with sunder all the time.
So you're hitting the backside of the foe and make a rotation 90% focused on keeping up a haste buff. Sometimes you can kick which is cool. But as I experienced, most of the rogue's fun is suppoed to be stealthing around and doing huge damage from a well-planned opening. Try this in a dungeon where the tank feels like being on cocaine and the hunter somehow pulls half of the region. At the end of the day dungeoning felt really boring. Looking for mobs' backside, auto-attacking. Sinister strike, auto-attack, keeping up haste, LF other enemy backside.
And your own professions... On paper sounds cool. In practice you need a reagent or material for everything. A rogue wants to shít, he needs a reagent to do it I swear. For example poisons are cool. But you make your doses in advance using materials and they expire super fast. On my enh shaman I just selected the weapon enhancement I liked and pressed it every 5 minute. You want to use half of your abilities? Reagent. You want to look like an orc peon? Materials. Every time you make the costume. Only lockpicking is different which just requires some tools to be in your bag. And also spending one of your Friday nights in a ship in the Barrens, interacting with a set of chests.

People also kinda boo internally every time you show up at the dungeon. Good damage, sure. But palas/shamans bring super buffs, a mage gives int, water, sheep etc, even a hunter can use traps. As a rogue you go to a dung 'bufflesly' and also rival most tanks at items. (I mean palas and warriors at weapons, drus at some leather items).

From raiding, I only heard about it. In theory it's chill with an easy rotation. But also, rogue is the only class which has no real upside at raids after BWL. From AQ40 a fury warrior is almost always better.

Again, for PVP I have no idea.

author: Edgarek
subject: A new rogue changes and my personal opinion about this
content_md:
**First, big thanks for adding axes to rogues. More gear options is always good.**
Ghostly Strike is now baseline, learned at level 20.
Heightened Senses is now baseline being learned at level 30, but no longer reduces your chance to get hit by attacks. Its stealth detection increase is equal to the fully talented version of the Subtlety talent.
Sinister Strike’s Energy cost is reduced from 45 to 40.
Sprint and Evasion’s cooldown reduced from 5 minutes to 4 minutes.

 **Good changes, just to make rogue live easier. Combat rogue now has 2.5 min cd for evasion and sprint.**
New Poison: Corrosive Poison:
Each strike has a 30% chance of poisoning the enemy for X Physical damage over 12 sec. Stacks up to 5 times on a single target. 105 charges.

 **Good. Might be useful and we get more damage, since poisons and WF totems stacks now.**
New Ability: Deadly Throw
Finishing move that causes thrown weapon damage plus additional damage per combo point.

 **...uhh i doubt anyone would use it, since there is like 3 blue throwable weapons in the game.**
 *Wound Poison now reduces effectiveness of any healing by 5% per stack, stacking up to 5 times instead of reducing the target’s healing power attribute. All items that were crafted above the first rank are now obsolete and have been converted into the first rank.*

 **We might finally able to penetrate bear druids. Good.**
 *Crippling Poison (Rank 2)’s slow amount has been reduced from 70% to 60%.*

Why? Rogues cant anyway to keep distance without control, mostly used for kiting mobs and in PvP against warriors.No reason to justify that nerf.

Now lets talk about talents and what i think about it.

ASSasination: Remorseless Attacks: Duration increased from 20 seconds to 40 seconds.
Ruthlessness: Proc chance increased from 20/40/60% to 33/66/100%.
Improved Slice and Dice: Renamed to “Improved Blade Tactics” and the text has been changed to: “Increases the duration of your Slice and Dice and Flourish ability by 15/30/45%.”
Vile Poisons: Now requires 3 points instead of 5 points.
Improved Poisons: Now requires 3 points instead of 5 points.

 **QoL, improvements, slightly better talents.**
 *Throwing Weapon Specialization: Moved from Combat 5th row to Assassination 4th row. Now gives your Deadly Throw a 50/100% chance to interrupt the target for 3 sec.*

 **Still useless, since there is only 3 blue throwable weapons in the game and none of them are really good.**
 *New Talent: Taste For Blood (5th Row / 3 Points): Your Rupture ability increases your damage by 3/6/10%. The buff duration is equal to the damage over time duration regardless of successful application.*

Better for PvE, worse for PvP.
 9% additional damage for everyone was quite good in pvp, and kidney only has 20 seconds cd, so you can apply quite often.
New rupture talent would be useful, but i think its should be in the subtlety spec. More information at the end.
 *New Talent: Efficient Poisons (5th Row / 3 Points): Reduces the chance your poisons will be resisted by 4/8/12% and gives your poison applications a 15/30/45% chance to not consume a charge.*

 **I doubt any rogue would care about charges.**
 *Vigor: Moved up from the 7th row to the 6th row, now requires 2 points instead of 1 point and now gives a 50/100% chance to gain 5 Energy when applying a poison to your target. This effect can trigger only once every 8 sec.*

 **Its barely has effect, maybe you will get 1 sinister strike in 1-2 minutes. But if you deep in ASS spec, you will take it anyway.**
 *New Talent: Envenom (7th Row Capstone): Finishing move that increases your poison application chance and effectiveness by 25%.*

That sounds interesting on paper. But poison doesnt scale properly, so i doubt its would be useful outside of fresh 60 trying meme build.

Overall Assasination looks insteresting, but underwhelming.
First problem - every rogue in the raid need to maintain SnD 4-5 combo points, but in this spec you also need to maintain Envenom 5 combo and Rupture 5 combo. Thats insane amount of energy required and Vigor with Seal of Fate even with 40% crit chance doesnt help at all.
You need 180% energy for that, basically having Adrenaline Rush on default just to maintain those 3 finishers. Yea, i couldnt pick Rupture, but where i would find more damage, if i cant go deep combat?
Second - poisons doesnt scale at all or very badly. Therefore, damage is limiting.

My suggestion would be add better last talent like real blizzard Envenom, that consumes all poison stacks and deals damage or idk Blind doesnt breaks under other poison effects. Maybe reduce blind cd with it, or increase poison stacks to 10. Anything that would compete with Combat spec, without collecting numerous sets for energy restoration.
Right now, nobody would pick talents above tier 3 besides experimenting.
Also improved SnD duration should be extended to 50% at max 45 seconds and IEA should also increase duration to 45 second. That would give rogues more room for finishers. Please dont be afraid to give rogues more uptime, its wouldnt boost damage.
And Rupture just doesnt fit there, if Envenom would be new finisher, having to uptime 3 finishers at once would be impossible without having abnormal crit for Seal of Fate.

COMBAT: Improved Sinister Strike: Now baseline and therefore replaced by Swift Strikes, see Baseline Changes.
New Talent: Swift Strikes (1st Row / 2 Points): Increases your melee attack speed by 1/2%.

 **QoL change and based talent, i like it.**
 *Setup: Moved from Subtlety 4th row to Combat 3rd row.*

 **Still garbage. History said, its took 2 expansions for Blizzard finally upgrade this talent to 100% chance in WotLK, just to work properly.** Blade Flurry: Moved from the 5th row to the 3rd row, but no longer grants 20% attack speed baseline.
New Talent: Blade Rush (5th Row / 2 Points): Reduces the cooldown of your Blade Flurry by 30/60 sec. Your Blade Flurry now increases your attack speed by 5/10% for the duration.

 **Should be baseline for everyone and combat inproved BF have the same 20% speed increase. Otherwise its just makes combat spec superior having 1 min cd.**
Mace Specialization: Renamed to “Concussive Blows” and moved up from the 5th row to the 4th row. No longer grants weapon skill to Maces.
Close Quarters Combat: Now also increases the critical strike chance of Maces.

 **I dont use maces, so i cant say much, but combat spec hiding weapon skill deep in the skill tree is bad.**
New Talent: Surprise Attack (5th Row Capstone): A surprise strike that deals 120% weapon damage. Only usable after the target dodges. Awards 1 combo point.
(10 Second cooldown, 10 Energy cost.)

 **Overpower, but for rogues. Actually good filler button to press, would be insteresting if its could be triggered by low weapon skill.**
 *Aggression: Damage buff increased from 2/4/6% to 3/6/10%, now also includes Riposte and Surprise Attack.*

Boost to main ability. Good.

Combat overall isnt changed and would deal even more damage after update.

SUBTLETY Master of Deception: Merged into Camouflage. Camouflage: Moved from the 2nd row to the 1st row, now also reduces the chance enemies have to detect you in Stealth mode.
Heightened Senses: Now baseline, learned at level 30.
Initiative: Proc chance increased from 25/50/75% to 33/66/100%.
Ghostly Strike: Now baseline, learned at level 20.

 **Godbless this QoL improvement.**
 *Improved Ambush: Moved from the 3rd row to the 2nd row, now refunds 5/10/15 Energy if the Ambush does not critically strike.*

 **Ehh...whole point of this talent to increase Ambush crit and combine with Remorseless Attacks for 85% crit chance increase in lvling Ambust/Backstab build. Not sure if it those 15 energy helps, but alright.**
 *Serrated Blades: Moved from the 4th row to the 2nd row. Now also increases the damage of your Garrote by 10/20/30% alongside Rupture.*

 **Even as combined talent, its still bad. 100 armor penetration and bleeds, if you can kill someone in pvp, you dont need bleeds, if you playing dungeons, most enemies dies way before your bleeds end. Garrote need invis and enemy back, and  most of the time you barely have enough time for the full duration of 1-2 points rupture.**
 *New Talent: Improved Ghostly Strike (3rd Row / 3 Points): Your Ghostly Strike has a 33/66/100% chance to increase your party members' chance to dodge by 3% for 7 sec.*

Now we getting to the talents that personally made me upset. It cant be stacked, its cant be used twice.
One question. Why? Why would anyone need 3% dodge? Who would move rogue in the tank group for 3% dodge chance with 1/3 uptime?

If you wanna help tank with dodge chance juju exists, its available on any class and could be used on range. I believe its also lasts longer.
New Talent: Smoke Bomb (3rd Row Keystone): Creates a cloud of thick smoke in an 8 yard radius around you for 8 sec. All targets inside the smoke have a 20% reduced chance to be hit by attacks and spells for the duration.
(5 Minute cooldown, 35 Energy cost)

Controversal talent, someone in discord mentioned its works on EVERYONE inside of smoke and its cant be stacked.
Thats includes 20% reduced chance to be hit by attacks and spells for enemies. For me its looks like a griefing tool, rather then meaningful safe. Also costs energy, so its cant be casted in the rotation.
Awful talent, unjustified cd.
Hemorrhage: Moved from the 5th row to the 3rd row, now only has one rank, grants 2% increased physical damage dealt instead of a flat value, amount of charges increased from 30 to 50, energy cost increased from 35 to 45 and now subject to weapon normalization.
New Talent: Bloody Mess (5th Row / 2 Points): Reduces the Energy cost of your Hemorrhage by 5/10 and increases the physical damage dealt bonus of your Hemorrhage by 50/100%

I feel very negative about that change. They basically nerfed already low sub rogue damage and its makes bleeds worse.
Every bleed tick got 7 additional damage from hemo, now its 4% physical, which means maybe 1-2 damage.
As for hemo himself, you need at least on average 175-200 white non crit damage, just to deal the same pre-nerf Hemo damage.
I guess 4% damage is good for fury warriors, but we talking about rogues - most selfish class in the game.
 *New Talent: Irritating Agent (4th Row / 3 Points): Reduces all damage dealt of targets hit by your Blind by 2/4/6% for 8 sec. This effect is guaranteed to be applied even if the target is immune to Poisons or Blind is resisted or misses.*

Why damage reduction...in a BLIND? 3 talent points for 6% damage decrease in 5 minutes ability, that eats consumable.
Rogues identity isnt to safe lifes, but brutally kill people by using dirty tricks.
Probably the worst talent introducted, its goes against rogue identity and doesnt add anything meaningful.
As for pvp, rogues arent relying on damage mitigation, but on stunlocks and burst damage, so developer comment doesnt know what he is talking about.
New Talent: Dust of Disappearance (5th Row Keystone): Throw a pouch of vanishing powder at a friendly player, reducing their threat by 20% and reducing the chance for enemies to detect their presence for 5 sec.
When the effect is cancelled or expires their next damaging spell or ability will deal 15% more damage.
(2 Minute cooldown, 30 yard range, 25 Energy cost, costs 1 Flash Powder.)

Good pvp talent. Could be used as save, if its applies invisibility, and 15% more damage could be huge for mages/warlocks.
In PvE 20% flat threat cut could be huge for warlocks. Dont know if 2 minutes cd is good tho, its either should be 1 min or its shouldnt cost energy, since other spell Vanish consuming same powder doesnt use energy for it.
 *New Talent: Honor Among Thieves (6th Row / 2 Points): Physical critical hits by party members within 20 yards grant you 2/5 Energy. This effect can only trigger once every 2 sec.*

 **Thats very conflicted talent, its sounds amazing, its can be insanely powerful, but at the same time its very limiting, its doesnt say YOU can trigger effect, make it useless for solo gameplay, and you need to be very nitpicky with teammates. I could be wrong, there was multiple times with the right ability description.**
New Talent: Tricks of the Trade (6th Row / 5 Points): Your opening and finishing moves have a 4/8/12/16/20% chance per combo point to increase your party's chance to critically strike by 2% for 10 sec. Stacks up to 2 times.
Developer Comment: This effect cannot be stacked by separate rogues and just refreshes the duration.

Bad talent in my opinion. By simple math at the start of combat, rogue has 100 energy and 100 energy in 10 seconds.
Now lets say you need to maintain SnD 5 combo with ass spec, you spend 175 energy, now you have 30 seconds to get another 5 combo points, so basically in order to maintain buff, you need rupture with 2 combo point, be lucky with 40% chance and SnD again.
All of that just to get 4% crit for a single party. At least another sub rogue with talent could help refresh it.
btw 160 dps 2 rogues, and 60 of that dps is poison, very effective dd, XD.
New Talent: Exploit Vulnerability (7th Row Capstone): A marking strike that deals 135% weapon damage and informs your party members of the target's vulnerabilities, increasing their damage dealt to the target by 15% for 6 sec. Awards 2 combo points.
(3 Minute cooldown, 40 Energy cost)

I cant express how upset i am with this talent.
Not only its has huge cd, short duration, its also cost energy and requires a melee strike and its buffs damage on a single target for a single group.
While old Premeditation 2 min cd, no energy cost, can be casted from invisibility on 20 range and had his niche in pvp builds.

What we got from Subtlety skill tree? One skill buffs 3% dodge, other decrease 6% damage, third skill increase 4% physical damage, fourth decrease agro/boost 1 attack, fifth limiting group composition, but boost energy gain... What that spec suppose to do?

Its has some damage increase tools, but mostly by Hemo(which was before), and Tricks of the Trade aka 4-5 combo spammer every 10 seconds for 2-4% crit, which is hella unrealistic, but everything else its just mishmash of different meaningless talents, that does nothing and main ability has been nerfed.
Active abilities are so balanced, they wasnt worth it investment deep in the tree, other passives are barely does something.

My suggestion would be to split old hemo and new hemo. then cut all of that 3% stupid group dodge that cant be even stacked, and commit to bleeds/damage boosts and stuns. Its still a main pvp spec after all, so give us tools for pvp.

Thanks for reading my banter, i hope my message reach developers and they at least do some changes. Right now, its looks like changes has been made without developers playing rogue or had any clue what that class does.

What we got from Subtlety skill tree? One skill buffs 3% dodge, other decrease 6% damage, third skill increase 4% physical damage, fourth decrease agro/boost 1 attack, fifth limiting group composition, but boost energy gain... What that spec suppose to do?

Its has some damage increase tools, but mostly by Hemo(which was before), and Tricks of the Trade aka 4-5 combo spammer every 10 seconds for 2-4% crit, which is hella unrealistic, but everything else its just mishmash of different meaningless talents, that does nothing and main ability has been nerfed.
Active abilities are so balanced, they wasnt worth it investment deep in the tree, other passives are barely does something.

My suggestion would be to split old hemo and new hemo. then cut all of that 3% stupid group dodge that cant be even stacked, and commit to bleeds/damage boosts and stuns. Its still a main pvp spec after all, so give us tools for pvp.

Thanks for reading my banter, i hope my message reach developers and they at least do some changes. Right now, its looks like changes has been made without developers playing rogue or had any clue what that class does.

Thats includes 20% reduced chance to be hit by attacks and spells for enemies. For me its looks like a griefing tool, rather then meaningful safe. Also costs energy, so its cant be casted in the rotation.
Awful talent, unjustified cd.
Hemorrhage: Moved from the 5th row to the 3rd row, now only has one rank, grants 2% increased physical damage dealt instead of a flat value, amount of charges increased from 30 to 50, energy cost increased from 35 to 45 and now subject to weapon normalization.
New Talent: Bloody Mess (5th Row / 2 Points): Reduces the Energy cost of your Hemorrhage by 5/10 and increases the physical damage dealt bonus of your Hemorrhage by 50/100%

I feel very negative about that change. They basically nerfed already low sub rogue damage and its makes bleeds worse.
Every bleed tick got 7 additional damage from hemo, now its 4% physical, which means maybe 1-2 damage.
As for hemo himself, you need at least on average 175-200 white non crit damage, just to deal the same pre-nerf Hemo damage.
I guess 4% damage is good for fury warriors, but we talking about rogues - most selfish class in the game.
New Talent: Irritating Agent (4th Row / 3 Points): Reduces all damage dealt of targets hit by your Blind by 2/4/6% for 8 sec. This effect is guaranteed to be applied even if the target is immune to Poisons or Blind is resisted or misses.
Why damage reduction...in a BLIND? 3 talent points for 6% damage decrease in 5 minutes ability, that eats consumable.
Rogues identity isnt to safe lifes, but brutally kill people by using dirty tricks.
Probably the worst talent introducted, its goes against rogue identity and doesnt add anything meaningful.
As for pvp, rogues arent relying on damage mitigation, but on stunlocks and burst damage, so developer comment doesnt know what he is talking about.
New Talent: Dust of Disappearance (5th Row Keystone): Throw a pouch of vanishing powder at a friendly player, reducing their threat by 20% and reducing the chance for enemies to detect their presence for 5 sec.
When the effect is cancelled or expires their next damaging spell or ability will deal 15% more damage.
(2 Minute cooldown, 30 yard range, 25 Energy cost, costs 1 Flash Powder.)

Good pvp talent. Could be used as save, if its applies invisibility, and 15% more damage could be huge for mages/warlocks.
In PvE 20% flat threat cut could be huge for warlocks. Dont know if 2 minutes cd is good tho, its either should be 1 min or its shouldnt cost energy, since other spell Vanish consuming same powder doesnt use energy for it.
New Talent: Honor Among Thieves (6th Row / 2 Points): Physical critical hits by party members within 20 yards grant you 2/5 Energy. This effect can only trigger once every 2 sec.
Thats very conflicted talent, its sounds amazing, its can be insanely powerful, but at the same time its very limiting, its doesnt say YOU can trigger effect, make it useless for solo gameplay, and you need to be very nitpicky with teammates. I could be wrong, there was multiple times with the right ability description.
New Talent: Tricks of the Trade (6th Row / 5 Points): Your opening and finishing moves have a 4/8/12/16/20% chance per combo point to increase your party's chance to critically strike by 2% for 10 sec. Stacks up to 2 times.
Developer Comment: This effect cannot be stacked by separate rogues and just refreshes the duration.
Bad talent in my opinion. By simple math at the start of combat, rogue has 100 energy and 100 energy in 10 seconds.
Now lets say you need to maintain SnD 5 combo with ass spec, you spend 175 energy, now you have 30 seconds to get another 5 combo points, so basically in order to maintain buff, you need rupture with 2 combo point, be lucky with 40% chance and SnD again.
All of that just to get 4% crit for a single party. At least another sub rogue with talent could help refresh it.
btw 160 dps 2 rogues, and 60 of that dps is poison, very effective dd, XD.
New Talent: Exploit Vulnerability (7th Row Capstone): A marking strike that deals 135% weapon damage and informs your party members of the target's vulnerabilities, increasing their damage dealt to the target by 15% for 6 sec. Awards 2 combo points.
(3 Minute cooldown, 40 Energy cost)
I cant express how upset i am with this talent.
Not only its has huge cd, short duration, its also cost energy and requires a melee strike and its buffs damage on a single target for a single group.
While old Premeditation 2 min cd, no energy cost, can be casted from invisibility on 20 range and had his niche in pvp builds.

What we got from Subtlety skill tree? One skill buffs 3% dodge, other decrease 6% damage, third skill increase 4% physical damage, fourth decrease agro/boost 1 attack, fifth limiting group composition, but boost energy gain... What that spec suppose to do?

Its has some damage increase tools, but mostly by Hemo(which was before), and Tricks of the Trade aka 4-5 combo spammer every 10 seconds for 2-4% crit, which is hella unrealistic, but everything else its just mishmash of different meaningless talents, that does nothing and main ability has been nerfed.
Active abilities are so balanced, they wasnt worth it investment deep in the tree, other passives are barely does something.

My suggestion would be to split old hemo and new hemo. then cut all of that 3% stupid group dodge that cant be even stacked, and commit to bleeds/damage boosts and stuns. Its still a main pvp spec after all, so give us tools for pvp.

Thanks for reading my banter, i hope my message reach developers and they at least do some changes. Right now, its looks like changes has been made without developers playing rogue or had any clue what that class does.
I COMPLETELY agree! In no way do I want to accuse the developers, and I want to congratulate them on the monumental work they’ve done! Great job, keep it up!
But when it comes to the Rogue class, this is not the class you’re trying to make it into right now! This is not a support class, and it’s not supposed to be the savior class! This is a class of damage and trickery in PvP! The only thing it should do well is deal damage! Bring back its guts!
topic_title: A new rogue changes and my personal opinion about this

author: Redmagejoe
subject: Re: Combo Points
content_md: Combo points are kept on Target A when you switch to Target B, but unlike vanilla, when you switch back to Target A, the points are no longer lost.  You cannot transfer your Combo Points to Target B, and if you apply a Combo Point to Target B, your points on Target A will be lost.

author: Resnica
subject: A fiery greeting to all Rogues of Azeroth!
content_md:
I don’t know how it came to this, but after the latest patch, the situation for you, my fellow Rogues, is truly dire! I’m really sorry that our once-amazing PvP class has been turned into a disgraceful shadow of an assassin. Yes, it still kills, yes, it still controls… but I assure you, compared to all the upgrades, nerfs, and buffs of other classes, the Rogue has remained almost unchanged—or even weaker than before!

The idea of a support Rogue is interesting… but that’s no longer a true Rogue! Especially in the Horde and especially in the late game, the PvP situation is awful! The balance in PvP is completely off.

That being said, I truly appreciate the dedication, vision, and hard work of the Turtle WoW team—I just hope Rogues get the attention they deserve!

author: Bigbosc
subject: End Game Rogues vs Warriors
content_md:
Currently end game Rogue is simply outclassed by DPS Warrior.  This kinda sucks for a few reasons.

First if we compare the DPS on both several cleave friendly fights like Anubrekhan, and on single target fights like patchwerk we can see around an 18% DPS difference with Warriors beating Rogues at all tiers of play.  I compared the number 1 warrior to the number 1 rogue, the same for number 20, number 50, and number 100 where applicable, over the last few months of logs from top guilds.

In all these cases the figure is at or close to 18%.  That sucks.

Please nerf warrior a bit and please buff Rogue a bit.  Maybe start with some simple numbers changes, like increase backstab, and sinister strike AP coefficient by 5% and nerf the coefficient on some warrior button, maybe execute?

DPS warrior is very similar in role in a raid to a rogue.  We are both physical dps who can field a number of useful armor debuffs, and other buffs (if rogue is sub anyway).  And we both offer mana free cleave damage, and strong single target damage.  We both offer solid interupts to enemy cast.  Finally we each have some unique abilities to help a raid, Warriors have some nice long cooldowns like Recklessness, Shield Wall, AOE taunt, etc.  Where rogue can help with some skips by using distract, or we can access 4 trinkets on a fight with vanish, or avoid certain mechanics like Webspray on Maexxna.

So the classes are pretty similar, and an 18% difference in output in every type of fight just sucks.  Thanks devs, I think Rogue is actually very fun right now and the designs are dope, but this difference needs some more numbers adjustments when possible.

author: Bigbosc
subject: Envenom Raiding could use some love
content_md:
I have been raiding on every spec rogues can field for the last few months, and testing thoroughly on end game content.  I have near bis for almost every set up, and have been clearing the end game for around 2 years now.

With that experience I have come to see that Envenom builds are not quite up to snuff with Combat builds, and both can certainly field Improve Expose Armor, which is our best buff, so there isn't much reason to play Assassin over Combat.

With the great change to poisons to have a scaling component, the gap between the two shrunk, Assassin got much better!  Awesome change, and another buff was given to Relentless Strikes to add a stacking finisher move damage buff.

Envenom spec (especially using backstab), can't really use Rupture or Eviscerate often.  I find the best DPS comes from 4 or 5 point Envenoms and 4 or 5 point Slice and Dices, which doesn't leave much room to push Rupture or Evsicerate almost at all, even during long fights.

This is a shame because the Rupture talents are really cool (taste for blood, serrated blades), and the change to Relentless Strikes is really cool too.  But if you can't really afford to push Rupture much at all, you get no benefit from this damage effect, and can barely get value from taste for blood or serrated blades rupture boost.

This is less of a problem if you are using sinister strike with your envenom build, but it still is a problem.  Its even worse of a problem if you are using Expose Armor for your raid benefit, you then simply can't ever push a damaging finishing move.  So all those cool talents are useless, and the relentless strikes buff doesn't affect you at all.

So I suggest we make a change to the Assassination talent tree.  Efficient Poisons says it reduces your chance for a poison resist, and gives a chance to not lose a charge.  A bit of an underwhelming talent, I suggest giving the resist part of this talent to Vile Poisons, just add it on, and give the charge part to Improved Poisons.  This is nice as the chance to not be resisted makes sense if your poisons are VILE!  It also has good synergy, if you take improved poisons your poisons trigger more often, and eat up charges faster, so making that talent also improve charge use is nice.

Next I would add a new talent where efficient poisons was "Singular Focus : Whenever you use a finishing move on a target afflicted by Envenom or Slice and Dice, you have a 33/66/100% chance to refresh the duration of those abilities.".

TL;DR  Assassination lags behind combat in DPS especially in cleave, and lags far behind Sub in terms of what it brings to a raid.  Give it some more fun buffs that help it in longer single target fights.  Adding a way to refresh the duration of Slice and Dice and Envenom, will free us up to be able to press expose armor, and damaging finishing moves more often.

author: Unsilentstorms
subject: The role of Subtlety
content_md:
as a sub rogue player, I thought I'd address some things that I noticed in both the talent trees and from the statements in one of the patch notes listed:
 ------------
"Rogue has a specialization that works fine aside from a few pain points, one that’s spot-on flavor but falls short gameplay-wise and one that lacks proper identity and tools especially in a raiding environment"

"This specialization lacks both identity and falls off in performance in raiding environments due to not being able to use their openers after their stealth and vanish are spent. We’ve considered abilities that would solve this such as Shadow Dance but after lengthy talks the conclusion was that Rogue did not need another flavor of dealing damage, and we’ve gone ahead with quite a different approach: a specialization that focuses on supporting their allies."
 -------------
The issue is that people are trying to look at the specializations in terms of an "identity" and not for what they actually are. Each class in the game have abilities comprising of 3 different categories. In this case, execution based abilities are assassination, toe-to-toe combat and defensives are 'combat' where as subtlety revolves around enhancing underhanded trickery and its efficiency.

To me it seems the talents in subtlety are mildly neutered, with core talents removed and made baseline with other talents placed at the convenience of an assassination / combat rogue for more DPS. but subtlety was not about just catering purely to some PVE play style, since it had PVP emphasis taking into account the nature of the game world and the various playstyles that can emerge to account for. It's about having a set up advantage, and emphasizing benefits from it's ability to exploit its foes (by way of getting openers, better stealth, dodging/avoiding, and preparation to get an extra set up) which is why making Heightened sense base line and merging camouflage with master of deception is not a good idea, and explains why it lacks identity.

And then at the expense of the spec, they allow easier access to improved ambush, serrated blades and hemo. That just sort of minimizes what subtlety has to offer by giving people an easy 5 points and another 3-6 to get all the main benefits out of the spec. -- where as if I want to get the most benefits out of assassination, I need at least 10 points. it would be like just dropping lethality/relentless strikes, or vile poisons into the second tier.

The idea as asssassin or combat is favoring opportunity to get camouflage so that you have the better CD and speed with more damage with less effective stealth.

Removing the Setup talent also nerfs the whole rogue tanking concept similar to a D&D style Duelist that you'd get paired with combat talents focused on a more regular use of ghostly strike with riposte and dodge talents. but this obviously could clash exploiting an abundance of dodges through abilities like smoke bomb + evasion + ghostly strike to build Combo points.

Hemorrhage actually boosts all sources of bleed damage to a target, even by group/raid members, and is where sub is meant to see its PVE DPS enhancement. and deadliness increased 10% attack power which increases your bleed damage

heightened awareness should remain as a talent with ghostly strikes and setup. there should be no dust of disappearance, smoke bomb or tricks of the trade or irritating agent, blinding haze, improved ghostly strike, honor among thieves. just seem pointless ineffective abilities no one is going to take anyway to play a sub raid spec or PVP spec when they can just get all the benefits of being combat or assassin with hemo and serrated blades improved ambush. and they also purely rely on a party.
 ------------------------------

Imo Feint needs to be improved. There should be more functionality around it and the talent sleight of hand. like making dodge chances during feint reduce your chance to be critically struck, or chance to avoid AoE or reduce it's damage like in retail - also similar to TBC's enveloping shadow talent. Improved sap should get similar functionality to Dirty Tricks talent.

Alternatively to irritating agent you can have sap/blind fades causing enemy to miss more often for a short duration.

now I don't know what DPS ratio's and rotations are looking like in this server yet. but I think the cata rotation had a nice feel. you set up to get in with the energy regen from slice and dice, enhanced damage on your bleeds, and chances to refresh your rupture on eviscerates.

In a similar way, the honor among thieves talent should be replaced with a similar energy regen without a party requirement, like either from bleeds ticking, damaging bleeding targets, or a slice and dice fairly balanced. this could also incentivize sub to go for an improved slice and dice for convenience.

The point overall is that some of these decisions don't seem very sensible and I think this approach can be revisited

Yeah. and there's a number of ways they can deal with this. I for one, like the shadow dance concept but I don't think the execution of it.

Shadowdance itself is based off the D&D Shadowdancer subclass that uses "Hide in Plain Sight" (also shadow clones) where periodically you can use this ability to re-enter stealth and get an attack off. but the issue with this is rogues already have it (vanish) and to further support it with preperation for a second use. and imo playing around with this feature could potentially make it a useful DPS rotation skill.

For example, you can have a raid talent that works similar to honor among thieves, but lowers the cool down of preparation so that you can get more vanish procs in a raid fight (although this could interfere with group PVP).

Or you can simply have a shadowdance ability that only let's you stay in stealth for 1-2 seconds without breaking combat so you can't sap with limited time to execute an ability, without the entering and re-entering stealth multiple times mechanic as it originally did, and make it only proc occasionally on CD from certain conditions.

Another alternative is an ability like shadowstep where it can have a talent proc to automatically cast ambush out of stealth similar to shadowstrike. making it so you'd want to save your shadowstep use for those procs.

These all seem to me pretty simple ways to get the benefits of the in stealth set up rotation into longer fights while limiting their use so that they are not too heavily abused for PVP situations

author: Ergoeht
subject: FNG takes a "stab" at balancing Rogue talents
content_md:
Hey all, long time WoW player, new to Turtle-WoW, and relatively inexperienced rogue offering his opinion that nobody asked for. I've seen a lot of legitimate concerns about how Rogue talents have been built. Ok here goes:

 1) Swap positions of Improved Blade Tactics and Improved Backstab.

Justification: IBT strikes me as more sustained DPS (or evasion) and IB is bursty with combo point gen. They're in the wrong trees. Swapping them is pretty easy: same row, same point investment. Combat rogues that dip into Assassination and Assassination rogues that dip into Combat probably won't notice a difference, but Subtlety rogues that dip into either will find choices that fit the tree themes better.

 2) Move Taste for Blood into the Subtlety tree, replacing Irritating Agent (more on that below). New talent: "Poison Injector. Your poison damage is increased by 5/10/15% of your melee attack power." 3 Points.

Justification: I've constantly seen Rogues mention that poison damage does not scale very well, so this deep talent is to address that. 5/10/15% might be the wrong values, but it's the right concept. A single bleed-based talent in assassination seems out of place.

 3) Change Improved Ghostly Strike's effect to: "Your Ghostly Strike increases your chance to dodge by an additional 2/4/6%, and your party members' change to dodge by 2/4/6% for 7 seconds."

Justification: While I like the concept of the "support rogue", there shouldn't be talents for rogues that don't also help themselves. Also 3% is a pittance, considering GS's cooldown, a max of 6% party benefit seems reasonable. This might make them a little too dodgy in PvP though (I'm not much of a PvP'er).

 4) Change Smoke Bomb to either not affect ALL targets, or to be a throwable AOE effect.

Justification: Either a lazy QoL improvement, or a more controllable skill shot if you place it well. Both fix the problem of it currently being just a mass "slowww it down here boys" effect.

 5) Get rid of Irritating Agent (mentioned above) and replace it with Taste for Blood from the Assassination tree.

Justification: Subtlety has other bleed-boosting talents, and could really use a good source of damage increase for the  spec.

 6) Change Blinding Haze to: "Targets affected by your Distract are 1/2/3% more likely to be hit, and 1/2/3% more likely to be critically struck, for 5 seconds. This effect is guaranteed to be applied"

Justification: A small damage boost for openers, helping those who aren't hit-capped yet a bit more, and still giving a little to those who are hit capped. The loss of defensive benefit is already compensated for in the changes to Improved Ghostly Strike above.

 7) Add the following to Mark for Death: "For the duration, abilities that ordinarily require stealth may be used against the target. May only be used against targets at least 3 levels higher than you." Remove the combo point generation. For flavor, perhaps rename the talent to "Slay the Goliath".

This gives a few windows in long fights to reapply garotte, hit ambush a few times, and reapply distract. Since you'll likely be getting a ton of combo points from openers, there is no need for it to generate points itself. It's unclear in the current tooltip whether to rogue benefits from the 15% damage boost themselves, but if they do, I don't think it's unreasonable to have a juiced opener spam mode in their rotation once every 3 minutes. The "3+ levels higher" restriction is so that it isn't horribly oppressive in PvP, although it does give sub rogues an interesting anti-overleveled-ganker niche in world PvP, no?

author: Finpin
subject: A Rogue PVE (DPS) Viability Analysis
content_md:
Hello everyone,

while this topic has been up for a while (yes Rogue are STILL in a very tough spot and would need some love) i want to highlight some issues Rogues currently have while giving feedback on the "buffs" to assassination tree from latest patch.

First and foremost: I feel that Rogues - while often underestimated - are a great and fun PVE class (I focus on dps rogue for now). They have different fun and also challenging rotations which vary from encounter to encounter.
Lore-wise I understand Rogues to be more of a melee glasscannon - leather armor, mitigation, high damage - high risk through dying easily when getting threat (no worries youll prob never draw threat under current circumstances).

The class varienty of Rogues in more or less limited. While turtle wow introduced changes to the Sub-tree giving rogues the possibility to be a supportive class, both other speccs (combat and assassination) are purely focused on damage output - DPS. As i didn't dive into Sub-rogue that much i can't say too much about its viability and usability and therefore want to focus on both other specs Combat and Assassination - the presumably most used specs for Rogues.

Around 90+% of Rogues players play Combat Spec, since its the (supposedly) most straight forward DPS spec. Rotations are more simple, you rely much on Blade Flurry and Adrenaline Rush to pump out damage for a short period of time. High weapon skill & hitchance help to put out a rather constant amount of damage - which is in current state rather mediocre dps IF you are not BiS'd out to the maximum. Logs are proving this over and over.
Yes - there are some outliers, but if you look at a broader distribution its clear rogues are nowhere near the top dps classes (single target OR aoe)

This might raise the question: SHOULD they actually be around top dps in PVE (as they were in vanilla back in the day) ?
If you ask me, they definitely should be around the upper end. Not only because i'd like to see them there but more simply because of of class design and lore. A lack of utility and variation should in my opinion go with a higher niche damage output. Rogue dont have raid buffs (dps rogues), rogues dont do massive aoe, rogues cant tank, rogues cant heal, rogues are not used for special mob mechanics in raids (apart from the lame example of supression room).

What can they do tho according to their first two skill trees?? Right, they can do DPS!
Unfortunately they are very bad at it right now though and therefore often seen as not very useful (e.g. "lets just take another warrior instead")

So Combat Rogues right now are pretty much just "meh". They are OK but not very strong in particular - every warrior (although i dont like to make comparisons to overclocked classes) does more damage while having more utility/variety (TANK, Single-target DPS, AOE DPS)

How about Assassination?

I liked that turtle wow devs tried to come up with some buffs for the assassination tree. Since then i actually thoroughly tried and tested the specc in different variations to compare possible damage output to standard-combat rogues and also to just find out if the adjustments bring rogues to another level in terms of DPS.

Long story short: Assassination does some decent damage right now and potentially more than combat spec.
Poison proc chances can be held at a high % and you can proc instant poison a lot which become a big part of your dps.
....................**BUT**........................... and here is the big BUT...........................
there are 2 big issues i noticed while raiding for a while using Assassination spec.
 1. The specc needs a lot of setup before you can get to your full damage output potential.
You need to have S&D and Envenom up, means you need to do 2 finishers before you do any damage at all.
This is not too bad since it makes the rotation simply more challening, you need to plan out more how you engage fights, especially quick ones. But i often find myself having S&D + Env up when the boss is on 70% already (Backstab/Sinister strike into 1 cp s&d - same for envenom)
You might imagine how it is with Trash packs. you basically use one mob to acivate each since they just die to quick.
While i feel this is generally OK since its just a more challenging approach - the damage output you get still simply does not compensate for the setup and "planning" you need. You basically have to work much harder to be on par with a shitty geared warrior or a melee hunter with similar gear - Im talking Single target dps right here.

 2. The second issue i have and this is the MUCH BIGGER one is Poison-Resistance of mobs and Bosses.
So as mentioned you have to work a lot harder to be on par in dps BUT now resistances come into play. While other melee classes do physical damage which always works, assassination rogues do 40% nature magic damage.
There are SO MANY bosses and Mobs that are simply immune to poisons which completely negates all the efforts you took to be on par in dps. ALL Elementals and other partly magic immune creatures/bosses (e.g. emperors, 50% of mc bosses) will just eat your poisons for lunch and be not affected.
Now some might say "Hey just use corrosive poison, its physical damage and will compensate" but this is simply not true.
Poison rogues kinda work because they proc so much (instant poison). Using corrosive poison you will stack to 5 and thats it. from that point on the poison ticks for a little damage for 12 seconds and all your procs (i have a proc chance of 65%, with totem from broodlord im at 95%) simply do nothing.
I am still filling the list of creatures and bosses where poisons are ineffective and the list gets bigger and bigger which gives poison rogues a really hard time.

This is my current feedback on DPS Rogues and primarily on the "new" Assassination rogue specc.
While i like the try from twow devs to adjust and make them more viable - IT IS SIMPLY NOT ENOUGH!

If you have more detailed questions on this, im happy to elaborate. I have done a lot of testing in terms of numbers etc. Though I might have missed stuff in here so feel free to give your input/question.

Happy over every input, thanks for reading

AND to the devs: PLEASE make rogues finally more viable so they are not the laughing stock of DPS classes anymore. They are a meme at this point which is sad cause the class is actually so much fun in PVE aswell.

Cheers

content_md:
As a player who plays mostly Subtlety PvE since forever, I can safely say Subtlety is the biggest looser atm. Plus the mob resistance issue you mentioned would not be as bad if you had an alternative. Now you basically cant take Seal Fate unless you go poison rogue which is kind of lame.

My partner plays rogue as when we were joining the game, Rogue Tank was advertised as a possibility through the Agitation Poison. So, he chose rogue both for that it was his first class back in OG Classic, and that he could still tank for me. He made this choice over a warrior, which sadly seems to have been the better choice long term both for damage and keeping agro from me (a holy priest). You never want to be bored while playing your main.

author: Sagabal
subject: Re: A Rogue PVE (DPS) Viability Analysis
content_md:
I was pleasantly surprised to see that Envenom amplified the cast delay of mind-numbing poison and the slow from crippling poison.  With that in mind, I wouldn't mind seeing the Assassination spec focus on utility over personal DPS similar to Sub's current direction, giving poisons bonus effects and ignoring poison immunity and so on.  That would however probably not be conducive to the playstyle currently developed with buff juggling, which probably just needs a buff to Vigor to be workable.  The other possibility is that it gets enough buffs until it's a viable pure DPS spec, and that would just mean that people who enjoy Combat may need to give up the playstyle they love to stay competitive, or would necessitate a change in direction for Combat with the same issue.

Rogue's always had a lot of unique issues as a class from their lack of utility/buffs/debuffs in a raid setting as well as their inflexibility in talent specialization, considering all their best talents are deep Combat.  I'm not surprised that there's a lack of clarity of direction, it's not an easy decision on where to take the class.  All of the suggestions they seem to get just seem to be in the vein of "Just make Assassination/Subtlety the good DPS spec!" so it's not like there's a lot of great feedback either.

Considering rogue tank, it could be another way of giving the class a new playstyle and direction, although considering last time it was in the game here I'm not sure how it could be reimplemented outside of something similar to how SoD did things, and I'm not sure how I feel about that implementation.  I like the idea but it would need way more fleshing out in terms of not only what niche it would fill but how it would even work.

author: Shananagans
subject: Re: 1.18 Blade Rush - Energy Regeneration?
content_md:
Blade Rush: Increases your melee attack speed by [2/5]% and reduces the time between energy regeneration ticks
by the amount equal to your agility. More effective than Blade Rush one.

A rogues energy regeneration (Baseline) is 20 energy every 2 seconds so, going from 0 energy to 100 energy will take 10 seconds. (baseline no buffs)

Blade rush as it states lowers the time of those ticks equal to the amount of agility.

(If I read this correctly): ( best Guess)

 1 agi = 1ms makes the most sense
anything smaller just wouldn't be worth putting points into. IMHO

From talent " and reduces the time between energy regeneration ticks
by the amount equal to your agility."

A rogue with 500 agility will lower the time between energy ticks by .5 seconds or (half a second).
Allowing the rogue to gain 20 energy every 1.5 seconds.

A rogue with 1000 agility will lower the time between energy ticks by a full second
Allowing the rogue to gain double the amount of energy within the same time period as the baseline amount.

Putting 2 points into Blade Rush only affects the attack speed element of the talent and not the energy tick regeneration.

At a certain point there will be diminishing returns, there is only so much agility you can pile on and ( for combat Daggers) Going over crit cap has to be monitored more closely than combat (unless your are running close to BIS gear)

There will be at times, adding attack power will be more beneficial than agility based on gear level.

IMHO (in my humble opinion) It's a must have talent for combat, regardless if you go swords, maces or daggers.( Out side of the Talent Adrenaline Rush ) it's the only way (not including gear) to get more energy regeneration back which = a smoother rotation which = more damage.

struggling to level/ Ambush, Backstab! Muhahaha!
or chose your own path, have fun and murder stuff!   turtle_in_love_head
Daggers for Life

JMHO but I think that diminishing returns are already baked into it in the way of not wanting to be or go over crit cap.
once you start getting above level 50, dungeon gear blues will start dropping for rogues that have a crit stat on it and on top of that are the talents that boost our crit.

ie Dagger rogues will get +5% crit putting 2 points into Close Quarter Combat, and another 5% crit for the talent Malice. If you went Backstab combat rogue you would then get another 30% increase to crit from Improved Backstab, and we haven't even started talking about agility on gear

If I remember right 1% crit is = to 29 agility, so 10% crit from just those 2 talents would = 290 agility

The gear I'm wearing now is the [Stormshroud Armor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=142%5B/url) which has 4% crit total on the entire set.

If you look at [Shadowcraft Armor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=184%5B/url) it comes with 157 agility which = 5.4% crit

And we haven't even started adding other gear like rings, neck, enchants.
This addon [Better Character Stats](https://github.com/pepopo978/BetterCharacterStats%5B/url) does have your boss crit cap already figured out based on your hit rating, expertise and other factors.

and here is the formula if you wana play around with it.

 100% - (base miss % - your hit %) - (base dodge %) - (base parry %) - (glancing blow %)
This only factors a 300 weapon skill, a higher weapon skill and the glancing blow % would change

I'm not sure if anyone can hit the crit hard cap on turtle wow. I do know at level 57 and the gear I had running Combat daggers at the time (Assassination now since 1.18) I was at my crit cap of 28%,( without buffs) If I was to get double agility enchants for my weapons it would have put me over then factor in + Kings buff + mark of the wild.

it is a balancing act with all the stats the higher your level and better your gear gets.

Like the Vigor talent on Assassination. Each time you apply poisons you have a 100% chance to gain 2 energy.

I have 1.3 daggers, with haste on gear I'm at 1.25 dagger speed, with slice and dice rolling I'm at .97 dagger speed and with the [Stormshroud Armor](https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?itemset=142%5B/url) Proc of 10% melee haste for 8 sec, I get down to .87 dagger speed. At this point IMHO adding more haste would just net me diminishing returns and get more damage by adding attack power or crit.

In a nutshell I agree with adding more agility, at a certain point will cause diminishing return as you said.
again this is JMHO

author: Jinkarasu
subject: Sub Rogue needs some love
content_md:
TL/DR in bold.

The changes and additions to the sub support tree seem pretty cool! I really like Shadow of Death and I think the consolidation of Imp Sap and the blinding debuff makes it a really solid talent.

 **The issue is the tightness of the Tricks of the Trade talent. At 12 seconds duration, this is unreasonable**. If a single hemo fails for any reason (miss, block, dodge, parry), or the finisher does for any reason, you drop the stacks. Additionally the timer requires you to spend 4 Hemos and 1 finisher (160-170 energy) every 12 seconds.

 12 seconds is 120 energy, accounting for Relentless strikes giving a refund, you're asking sub pve rogues to spend 160-170 energy with an energy income of 140. This means the energy talents must make up for it. Maybe in a highly optimized group for a raid, getting 5 energy every 1.5 seconds will actually pan out, and assuming every frame the cooldown is up there's a party physical crit to grant you the energy, this increases your energy income to 180.

Is the intent that this spec only feels good to play in a hyper optimized environment for raids? And only once you've acquired a minimum baseline of gear to ensure that nothing goes wrong rotationally? 4% crit isn't huge, but the upkeep on the buff being on such a tight timer really conflicts with the rest of the kit.

This barely holds together just using hemorrhage and expose armor and slice n dice. You gave us shadow of death, but the 30 energy cost means dropping the tricks stacks. Using distract means dropping the tricks stacks. Using smoke bomb drops the tricks stacks. Gouge drops the stacks. Blind drops the stacks. Kicking a spell drops the stacks.

You gave us support tools and then made the timer on this so tight that we're not allowed to use our support tools.
What's more is this talent REQUIRES ruthlessness and relentless strikes to be functional.

 ***Please make it last 30 seconds. Maybe 20 seconds minimum.***

Maybe gear fixes this, but I find it hard to believe that they want such a high gear check for an inconsistent 4% crit buff.

author: Asystol
subject: Re: Sub Rogue needs some love
content_md:
In addition to all said above, yes Sub rogue is a Supporter with buffs and slightly incoming dmg reduction cd`s.
There is also a possibility for a good rotation with Garrote/Rupture/Slice and Dice, but even if you force full concentration on this - the dmg output itself is too low.
Not talking about to reach the numbers, assa and combat are doing, but the dps loss for the benefits of sub comparing to other classes/speccs is definetly too high.

Maybe we could have an improvement in Serrated Blades from 30% to 50% for Garrote/Rupture.

OR

Merge Honor among Thieves with Tricks of the Trades (2+5 Talent Points is anyway a very high cost at the moment) and put another Talent in the position at Step 6 in Talent tree. Increase flat Weapon dmg or overall Bleeding dmg.

We could have three Talent trees, using mainly different types of dmg: Poison / Physical / Bleed

PS:
To be honest, Shadow of death does "OK" numbers, feels more like an uninspired emergency solution to push dps a bit. I do think this spell more "breaks" a smooth sub rotation, but you have to use it, to get at least a small peak in overall dmg.

author: Jinkarasu
subject: Re: Sub Support?
content_md:
So the largest, most consistent benefit is the 4% physical damage increase that hemorrhage grants the raid. As long as you're spamming hemo, that should never really fall off. Additionally the improved access to Improved Expose Armor means you have the largest armor drop in the game, to boost physical damage yet further.

Then for your specific party, you have Tricks of the Trade that grants 2-4% additional crit chance depending on if you have the gear and raid comp to get a full 5 point combo off every 12 seconds.

Additionally you have Mark for Death which buffs you and your party by a % of your attack power.

Defensively, sub has some interesting abilities. Blind is a 10% damage mitigation if talented for it. Distract lowers enemy accuracy. Having access to improved sap makes some dungeons way easier.

That said, sub feels like ass to play until you have the requisite hit cap, a sufficient amount of crit baseline to power the energy procs, a full 5 man melee party in the raid group to additionally facilitate said energy procs, and possibly shadowcraft's energy proc bonus. If you don't meet all those requirements you'll be stuck with the 2% crit buff and never able to push any buttons other than hemo, expose armor, and slice and dice.

author: SvenS2
subject: Rogue spec identity discussion
content_md:
So both in theme and gameplay what are they?

Judging by the talents alone they're like this for vanilla:

 **Assassination** - Boosts to Combo Finishers and Poisons. Thematically, the Poison rogue.
 **Combat** - Boosts to combo starting abilities out of stealth, with some PvP utility.
 **Subtlety** - Boosts to combo starting abilities while in stealth, with some PvP utility.

in TWoW it's mostly the same, with **Subtlety** being changed to have support utility as well.

Now that's a very high level overview, but these have always felt off (to me), and only in Wotlk did each spec start feeling more distinct and with a more focused intent. What I mean by this is, which is the PvP and which the PvE spec? Is it at all 3 or each has partial benefits to help with PvP and PvE. It's obviously the latter, but why? Doesn't that only make balancing each spec harder?

And as far as identity, why does Assassination have both Poisons and Combo Finishers as its gimmick? Wouldn't the Combo Finishers fit Combat rogue more? Their whole playstyle is pressing their 1 combo generating ability and spamming a finisher, so why not enhance that? Likewise, Assassination benefits from fast attacking weapons to proc poisons, so why not give dagger specialization to them instead? Or better yet Sub, since daggers are a "subtle" weapon opposed to swords and maces. Or what about Improved Backstab. That fits Sub's theme of sneakily doing damage a lot more than it does combat. And in terms of how damage is done, how are they defined? Assa is changed to be more DoT heavy thanks to Taste for Blood, but Serrated Blades is in the Sub tree. In the last patch, you could play Backstab Assa, and still pickup Serrated Blades, but with the talent changes that build path is significantly weaker

My own interpretation for ideal gameplay identity of these specializations has been:

Assassination = DoT damage and additional effects based on applied poisons.
Combat = Combo damage, expert in Swords and Maces.
Sub = Burst damage, and a lot of PvP utilities.

Of course, that's entirely my own point of view, and I'm not suggesting any changes in this thread. But I really want to hear your opinions on these specializations' identity. Be it gameplay or theme

author: Unclecatjam
subject: ...of class fantasy & niche concepts (Rogue)
content_md:
So..
I wanted to start a *(hopefully civil)* discussion about your ideas, concepts and thoughts in regards to class fantasy or identity, especially the niche ones. Examples for that would be something like the outlaw rogue, as a swashbuckling, pistol wearing subclass or SoD's time twisting, temporal healer mage subclass or maybe even the survivalist, trap-throwing meele hunter subclass.

This is soley meant as a fun little discussion and exchange of ideas and not a suggestion for TWOW *(even though, some ideas might be actually cool to see coming to life)*.

I'd like to start with the rogue forum mostly because I've always thought the talent trees were lacking in the department of identity and even after outlaw made it to retail, it never hooked me the way I was hoping for.

 **Assassination:** Out of the three available talent trees assassination is the only one that, in my opinion, has a real tangible class identity as the sneaky, murderous and backstabbing assassin. There's not a lot I'd change class fantasy-wise, other than moving over a lot of the subtlety talents to assassination (like camouflage, improved ambush and similar, sneaky, backstabbing talents).
 ***Assassin***

 **Lore Implementation:** Not needed, it's an Assassin - Ravenholdt or maybe SI:7

 **Combat:** Combat always felt weird to me, mostly because of the word in itself. Combat, to me at least, just doesn't feel rogue-ish enough, unless it is meant in the swashbuckling way. *"Cheating"* in open combat by throwing dust in your enemies eyes or leaving them flat-footed through deceit and feints. The retail version, namely the outlaw talent tree always felt too cartoon-ish to me. While rolling dice and shooting a blunderbuss point-blank seemed cool, to me it felt half-hearted and sluggish *(or maybe I'm just too stupid to play the class..)*.
Having said that, I'd always wanted the dueling type of swashbuckler (similar to the DnD 5e subclass) - that excels at 1v1 by blinding, taunting and parrying their enemies or throwing oil-filled bottles on the ground to catch them off-guard or otherwise cheat their way to victory. There's a lot of talents or skills that already hint in that direction, like riposte, blind, vanish, cheap shot, kidney shot, feint, distract or kick *(a kick to the groin style)*.
 ***Swashbuckler***

 **Lore Implementation:** Well, easy to implement.. Pirates are already a thing: Bloodsail Buccaneers, Blackwater Raiders or anything Booty Bay.

 **Subtlety:** Now here comes the niche idea that's been haunting me for quite a while because subtlety to me is just a small aspect of assassination, at least from my point of view... therefore it could wander over to the assassination talent tree and cut out the rest, that doesn't fit.
Let's talk about throwing weapons, which never got a fair chance. Often you read about the concept of a ninja talent tree which of course, as a class fantasy, sounds really fun, but... I personally could never figure out a way to implement them lore-wise that felt fitting and true to warcrafts lore, without just being a weeaboos wet dream *(no shade - love me some weeb-dom)*. So I had an idea and it ties in with the darkmoon faire of all things - let me introduce: the Jester, but more about that in the Lore Implementation section.
Gameplay could revolve around throwing weapons, which of course would have to work like bows, guns or wands first and foremost. Daggers or other weapons, would be statsticks and only used similar to the hunter meele weapon: only meant to slow, cripple and trip anyone that comes near you, so you can create distance to throw your knives at them.
You could, if the assassination tree would be filled to the brim, even implement the poison aspect here, but that's up for debate. Next to Deadly Throw, skills or talents like Fan of Knives, Ricocheting Throw or Poison Dart could be implemented as either finishers or combo point generators. This is of course a very vague concept, but I always liked the idea of a fully ranged rogue talent tree and not the half-assed version that is the retail outlaw.
 ***Jester***

 **Lore Implementation:** I am anticipating that I will lose a lot of you with this one, if I didn't already with the Swashbuckler, but nevertheless it is a niche concept that I personally really like: The (Court-)Jester or the Darkmoon Faire Specialist. Why the darkmoon faire? Well, throwing knives seems very fitting also (extended) lore wise, it wouldn't be too far off. Silas Darkmoon, the leader of the Darkmoon Faire is according to the comic Legends a fair and passionate leader, that isn't afraid of criminal activities if it means to protect his found family of weirdos and outcasts. Considering the story of the comic legend implementing the jester could look something like this:

> The Darkmoon Faire started as a gathering of misfits, lead by Silas Darkmoon. During the events in Southshore, where strong-woman Kerri Hicks was accused of murdering Cedrick Fallrooks brother, Erik Fallrook, who in fact was murdered by Cedrick himself, Silas took matters into his own hands by not just freeing Hicks out of jail, but also burrying Cedrick Fallrock alive. From this moment forward Silas swore to protect not just his own people, but all the common folk from injustice and the meddling affairs of nobility. His new found resolution led to the founding of the underground organization commonly refered to as "The Pale Moon Vigilantes".

This is all very far fetched, the name just pulled out of my arse and there's a million different ways to implement them or somthing similar (and maybe it's not even relevant that it's called the jester) but I really wish there would be a fully ranged rogue talent tree - as I've said multiple times already!

Well, this is already long enough and that's where I want to close my ramblings.

I'm curious and would love to hear about your ideas, concepts or class fantasies in general that stuck with you over the years warcraft has entertained all of us *(sometimes more, sometimes less)*.

So long and tudelu,
Catjam!

author: Shananagans
