content_md:
> **Haderan1 wrote: Sun Oct 26, 2025 5:15 pm**
> I'm level 35 and have been following your guide. Really solid so far, I have no complaints. Due to the nature of the increased rate of poison application, would you recommend sticking to instant poison on both weapons?
>
>  Also, based on your current recommendations, where would you put your final 2 talent points?
>  And finally what would be the rotation for level 50-60 with this build?

Glad you are enjoying it

Regarding poisons: Poisons are situational really. (jmho) Use 2 fast daggers and don't use any damage over time poisons ie. (Deadly, corrosive)

If you are fighting animals, beasts and the like, just go double instant until you get Dissolvent poison.

If fighting humanoids, orcs, trolls and the like, I would run instant on main hand and crippling on off hand.

In dungeons, it's your call, depending on what mobs it is that you are fighting and how spaced out are they from each other.

I'm sure you have notice that humanoids have a tendency to run when they get low on health, and by George we do not want them running away agroing more mobs lol.

Dungeon Rotation: Rotation is simple, you are going to try and open up on a mob from ambush,( since stealth is on a 5 sec cooldown, you should have time before each mob pack in dungeons to re-enter stealth). from there it's backstabbing till you get to 4 combo points then slice and dice and repeat.

Open World

I don't like sinister strike unless i absolutely have to use it.

Poisons: See above

What I do- Ambush into gouge, pool a little energy and pirouette to the back side and backstab.
I now have 3-4 combo points.

 1. how much health they have left, not much? Eviscerate, call it a day, get back in stealth and do it again.

 2. They have more health than I like, Check to see if crippling up on mob, rupture and kite (while lol-ing) as soon as rupture runs it course, gouge, pirouette to backside and backstab. if their not dead you should have 2-3 combo points to eviscerate to finish em off or rupture again and keep lol-ing :) so much fun being a rogue.

As rogues, we have alot in our tool box to use, like, blind, Kick, Gouge, Sap, using Vanish offensively ( don't use Vanish offensively when solo, it will rest the mob back to full health)

while kiting, feel free to work on your range weapon skill :)

A lot of stuff I have covered here [1.18.0 Rogue leveling spec](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=20993%5B/url)

At level 58, you should re-spec. What you re-spec to is totally up to you. I went Assassination and I am melting my Enemies

To see that check [Face Melting Fun](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?t=20585%5B/url)

I don't know everything, so get out there and experiment, kill stuff and have fun

Daggers for Life

Well as assassination the only requirement imo is being 40 for noxius assault and you MUST have poisons on weapons. The rotation is simple you usually choose to spend combo points in eviscerate or rupture depending if the mob is going to be alive for 10+ seconds or not. The perfect situation would be keep rupture on enemy, slice and dice on yourself and only then use eviscerate, but I never managed to do that. Lot of energy starvation in classic

In combat/sub you can go any weapon you like build differs slightly.
I usually go dagger sub (with few combat talents for backstab) when doing dungeons (and if i raid too) since I can always backstab enemies easy. The improved backstab talent (combat) enhances crit chance and gives a chance to get 2 combo points I think it's is huge but then again if you are solo leveling it's kinda shit to frontstab enemies.

With non-dagger sub you definitely want to focus on hemo talents and ignore improved backstab and improved ambush for obvious reasons.

In any case I do not recommend going full sub if you are solo leveling some big talents rely on your party or are better in party (tricks of the trade, shadow of death, honor among thieves, mark of death). You could build sub until hemorrage and then swap to combat talents for example

My issue is people who have clearly never played an energy class before completely blowing the whole thing out of proportion.

First and foremost, poison damage scaling has not actually changed between now and the last patch, the primary difference is noxious assault and envenom being added to the talent tree. However in a pvp scenario, a rogue is unlikely to have the spare time, energy, or combo points to pull up envenom, so that is basically off the board entirely.

Additionally, if a rogue is specced into noxious assault, that means they DONT have dirty deeds OR preparation. This means their cheap shot is 60 energy, not 40.

So in a full stunlock combo, they will AT MOST, manage to get off 3 noxious assaults in a cheap shot/kidney combo:

 60 energy 4 second stun cheap shot -> 4 second stun = 2 energy ticks, so they get to 90 energy (sin rogues have 110 energy) meaning they can pop 2 noxious assaults, however then they wouldn't have any energy left over for a kidney, so they need to cheap shot -> noxious assault -> kidney shot at 4 combo points, meaning they lose out on a 6 second kidney, and instead only get a 4 second. That's 2 more energy ticks, with an 80% chance to refund the kidney, so they get at most another 40 energy up from the 45 they were at, giving another 2 noxious assaults, and being left at 3 combo points.

Now each noxious assualt does approximately 300-400 armor-affected damage, plus two lots of 250ish poison damage (probably less due to envenom not being up), so about 800 damage total against an armored opponent. You get three of those off in a full cheap shot/kidney combo, if you leave yourself 0 energy afterwards for a blind. That's 2400 damage, plus auto attacks. Since the stunlock is 8 seconds, and we assume 1.3 speed daggers, that's 12 autos at 30% proc chance each, so about 3-4 more poisons, so another 750-1000 damage.

So you'll end up taking ~3150 - 3400 damage total. Yes that's a lot. Except the rogue is now at 0 energy. And you're not stunned. And if they blind you, you can trinket the blind. Because they're noxious assault spec, and don't have prep to re-blind. Also, you're not slowed, because they have dps poisons in both hands.

Now, I'm not really arguing for or against poisons and their balance in pvp, what I'm saying is: get your facts straight. 60 energy 4 second stun cheap shot -> 4 second stun = 2 energy ticks, so they get to 90 energy (sin rogues have 110 energy) meaning they can pop 2 noxious assaults, however then they wouldn't have any energy left over for a kidney, so they need to cheap shot -> noxious assault -> kidney shot at 4 combo points, meaning they lose out on a 6 second kidney, and instead only get a 4 second. author: Snoof
subject: Re: Poison Damage Busted in PVP
content_md: Letting a melee ignore armor just screws up any semblance of class balance PvP has. In PvP the story has always been that melees want to hit casters because they have low physical resistances and casters want to hit melees because they have low magic resistances. Melee classes are built around burst, so whenever you let one do full damage to other melees, they just become obnoxious one-shot machines that the other melees can't fight. It's the same reason enhancement shamans are so overbearing right now, except instead of one-shotting you while being mega tanks rogues do it while unplugging your keyboard.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Stealth seems to be broken (sometimes)
content_md:
Im only having limited experience as my rogue is still levelling. But here is my best guess whats happening and how you can deal with it.

Turtle wow serverticks are luch much faster than they were in classic wow (0.04seconds vs 0.4seconds)

That means in classic, even if the mob was technically so close he could spot you, foe up to 0.4 seconds he wouldnt yet react. On turtlewow you arent afforded that luxury. Similarly, If a mob notices you close but hasnt qute spotted you yet, he turn for you and will attack you if you dont back away quickly. This period of time seems to be much shorter too.

How do you stealth efficiently with this knowledge?
 1. Never stealth close to a mobs face. Their stealth detection facing forward is stronger than you expect because you have no grace period
Approaching from behind yields better results
 2. Use distract against mobs that might spin while you approach them
 3. Dont dick around in melee range. Shiftloot pickpoket and opener. Dont give the mob time to react.
 4. Never run trough the hitbox of a mob. No amount of stealth level hides you if you stand inside a mob
 5. Some mobs have very high stealth detection. Learn to avoid them. Typically packdogs/hyenas, mobs that dont rely on vision such as bats or mobs with tracker in their name have drastically increased stealth perception to the point where stealth can be entirely useless.

Wether stealth level works at all im afraid i cant tell either

author: Sslushee
subject: Thoughts on Going Assassination at Level 40
content_md:
Hey folks — just wanted to drop a quick note for anyone thinking about going Assassination around level 40.

I’ve been leveling daggers all the way up, with a short detour into Combat Swords. For context, I’ve been playing WoW for about 20 years now — my first toon was a rogue back in 2005 — so I’ve been around the block with this class.

That said, I’m only level 40 right now, so this post is focused entirely on leveling performance, not endgame.

![⚔️](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/2694.svg) What I’ve Found So Far

 **Combat (Swords):**
Easily the weakest option I’ve tried — and it’s not even close. Leveling as Combat felt rough enough that I swapped back to daggers after just a few hours. It’s nowhere near the powerhouse it was in vanilla.
Rogues themselves are strong… but this spec just doesn’t hold up while leveling.

 **Daggers (Sub/Combat Mix)**
This setup was decent, but not great. My basic flow was:

Ambush → Gouge → Backstab → Eviscerate

If Ambush or Backstab didn’t crit, the fight dragged on forever and usually ended with me bandaging. It worked, but felt inconsistent — solid burst, weak sustain.

 **Assassination** (Level 40 Respec)
When I hit 40, I was on the fence about switching — I thought I’d really miss Precision. Took the risk anyway, and man… I’m so glad I did.

Mobs are melting. I don’t miss Precision at all.

This build isn’t crit-dependent in the slightest — I even skipped Remorseless Attacks and have only two points in Seal Fate, which is working fine since the whole build revolves around poisons instead of crits.

Here’s the gist:

Grab all the poison talents + Efficient Poisons

Use two daggers (avoid swords, maces, axes). Faster = more poison procs.

Rotation looks like:

Cheap Shot → Envenom → Slice & Dice (off the Ruthlessness point) → Noxious Assault twice → Dead

Result? I’m killing mobs about 75% faster than I was with my Ambush/Backstab build. I’m also topping DPS meters in every dungeon since the respec — before this, I was usually mid-pack.

Build at 40:
![👉](//cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/twitter/twemoji@latest/assets/svg/1f449.svg) [https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue?po ... gDYZIQQB--](https://talents.turtlecraft.gg/rogue?points=AoYCIgDYZIQQB--)

If you’re on the fence about trying Assassination at 40 — do it. You won’t regret it.

Note: After extensive target dummy testing, double Instant poison (at least at 40) trumps both instant/deadly and deadly/deadly. Instant poison is hitting so fast that the 5 stack cap on deadly ends up hindering your dps.
